column3: Mouth. It began as a picture of an open mouth, and it brings eating, speaking and sounds. It usually sits on the left, sometimes inside or beneath other parts. Examples: 吃 eat, 喝 drink, 吗 question particle, 哪 which. Many spoken particles such as 吗 and 呢 carry it as the "mouth" clue; in 哥 and 同 it is only part of the shape.

A squeezed form of 人 (person), written on the left side. It marks people and what people do or are. Examples: 你 you, 他 he, 住 live, 做 do, 候 wait. In many of these it is simply the left part, and the sound often comes from the right-hand side.
A squeezed form of 水 (water), written as three drops on the left side. It brings water, liquids and flowing, and also wet or cool states. Examples: 洗 wash, 渴 thirsty, 涼 cool, 淨 clean, 溫 warm.

Tree or wood. It began as a picture of a tree with branches on top and roots below. Left side or bottom, it points to trees and wooden things. Examples: 杯 cup, 桌 table, 校 school, 楼 building. In 東, 果 and 来 it is only part of the shape.
A squeezed form of 手 (hand), written on the left side. It marks actions done with the hands. Examples: 打 hit, 拉 pull, 推 push, 接 receive, 換 change. In 找 and 报 it is just the dictionary radical.

A squeezed form of 辵 (walking), written along the bottom-left and wrapping under the rest. It brings movement, going and distance. Examples: 进 advance, 过 pass, 远 far, 边 side, 送 see off. In 這 it is the sound part, so it can mislead there.
Speech: talking, words and language. It is usually on the left, with 讠 as the form used in simplified characters (the same radical). Examples: 說 speak, 請 please, 謝 thank, 語 language, 認 recognize.
The simplified form of 言 (the same radical), written on the left. It brings speech, words and language. Examples: 说 speak, 请 please, 谢 thank, 语 language, 认 recognize.

Two different radicals share this shape, depending on the side. On the left it comes from 阜 (mound, hill): 院 courtyard, 隊 team. On the right it comes from 邑 (town): 都 all, 部 department, 那 that. Left means hill, right means town, but in many characters it is mostly a shape to file them under.
A squeezed form of 艸 (grass or plant), written across the top. It brings plants, herbs, flowers and food from plants. Examples: 菜 vegetable, 茶 tea, 草 grass, 花 flower, 藥 medicine.

Earth or soil. It began as a picture of a mound of earth. On the left or bottom, it points to ground, places and things built of earth. Examples: 地 ground, 場 field, 墙 wall, 塊 lump. In 坐 and 報 it is only part of the shape.
Heart, mind. It began as a picture of a heart. At the bottom it brings thoughts, feelings and will. Examples: 想 think, 忘 forget, 急 anxious, 意 thought, 思 think. Its squeezed form on the left is 忄.

A squeezed form of 糸 (silk thread), written on the left side. It brings thread, cloth, cords and knots, also colors. Examples: 紅 red, 綠 green, 紙 paper, 給 give, 結 knot. 纟 is the same radical in simplified characters.

A squeezed form of 竹 (bamboo), written across the top. It brings bamboo things, such as 筷 chopsticks and 籃 basket. Much more often it is just a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning: 第 order, 答 answer, 等 wait, 算 calculate.

Roof, house. It began as a picture of a house. Written across the top, it brings houses, rooms and shelter. Examples: 家 home, 室 room, 客 guest, 安 peaceful. In 寫 and 定 it is mainly a shape, and in 實 it is the sound part.
The simplified form of 糸 (silk thread), written on the left; the same radical as 糹 in traditional characters. It brings thread, cloth and colors. Examples: 红 red, 绿 green, 纸 paper, 给 give, 结 knot.
A squeezed form of 肉 (meat, flesh), written on the left. It looks like 月 (moon) but brings the body and its parts. Examples: 脑 brain, 脸 face, 腿 leg, 脚 foot, 胖 fat. In 能 it is only a shape.
Woman. It began as a picture of a woman. On the left or bottom, it brings women, family relations and female things. Examples: 妈 mom, 姐 elder sister, 妹 younger sister, 姓 surname, 婚 marry.
Sun, day. It began as a picture of the sun. On the left or top, it brings the sun, daylight and time. Examples: 時 time, 昨 yesterday, 晴 clear weather, 晨 dawn, 星 star. In 是 and 普 it is only a shape.

This is the number one, a single horizontal stroke. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning: 不, 三, 七, 上 and 下 are all filed here only because of the stroke. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

A squeezed form of 刀 (knife), written on the right side. It brings cutting and sharp things. Examples: 刻 carve, 別 separate, 剧 play. In 到 arrive it is the sound part, and in 前 and 利 it is only a shape.

Enclosure. It is a box drawn around the rest of the character, bringing the idea of surrounding or bounded places. Examples: 国 country, 园 garden, 围 surround, 回 return. In 四, 因 and 图 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Cloth, towel. It began as a picture of a hanging piece of cloth. On the left or bottom, it points to cloth things. Examples: 布 cloth, 帶 belt, 幣 currency. In 師, 市 and 希 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
A building with a roof, written over the top-left of a character. It brings houses, shops and rooms. Examples: 店 shop, 床 bed, 座 seat, 庭 courtyard, 廣 wide. In 度, 应 and 平 it is mostly a shape.
A squeezed form of 衣 (clothing), written on the left side. It brings clothes and cloth. Examples: 衫 shirt, 裤 pants, 裙 skirt, 袜 socks, 被 bedding.

In characters this means head. It began as a picture of the head of a kneeling person. Usually on the right. Examples: 頭 head, 顏 face, 領 neck, 顧 look back. By itself it now means page. 页 is the same radical in simplified characters.

A tapping or striking hand, written on the right side. It brings actions done to something. Examples: 教 teach, 放 release, 收 collect, 救 aid, 改 alter. In 整, 散 and 敢 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Eye. It began as a picture of an eye, now turned on its side. On the left or top, it brings the eye and seeing. Examples: 眼 eye, 睛 eyeball, 睡 sleep, 看 look. In 真, 直 and 相 it is mostly a shape.

It began as a picture of a right hand. As a radical it gives no clue to meaning: 友 friend, 难 hard, 发 issue, 受 receive and 反 reverse have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Strength, effort. On the right or bottom it brings strength and work. Examples: 动 move, 助 help, 努 exert, 办 set up, 势 power. In 加 and 功 it is the dictionary radical.
A squeezed form of 心 (heart), written on the left side. It brings feelings, thoughts and states of mind. Examples: 慢 slow, 怕 fear, 情 emotion, 懂 understand, 慣 habit.
Fire. It began as a picture of a fire. On the left it brings fire, heat and burning; at the bottom it is written 灬. Examples: 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke, 烧 burn, 烤 bake, 煩 bother.

A squeezed form of 金 (gold, metal), written on the left side. It brings metal, money and metal objects. Examples: 錢 money, 鐘 clock, 鐵 iron, 銀 silver, 鎖 lock. 钅 is the same radical in simplified characters.

A squeezed form of 火 (fire), written as four dots along the bottom. It brings fire, heat and cooking. Examples: 热 heat, 熟 cooked, 照 shine, 烈 fiery. In 為, 無 and 烏 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Ear. It began as a picture of an ear. On the left or top, it brings hearing and sound. Examples: 聽 hear, 聞 news, 聲 sound, 聰 sharp, 聊 chat.

Shell, money. It began as a picture of a cowrie shell, which was used as money. On the left or bottom, it brings money, trade and value. Examples: 買 buy, 賣 sell, 貴 expensive, 費 expenses, 貨 goods. 贝 is the same radical in simplified characters.

Grain. It began as a picture of a plant stalk. On the left, it brings crops. Examples: 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 種 kind, 積 store up. The link is often loose; in 科 and 称 it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Stone. It began as a stone beneath a cliff. On the left, it brings stone and rock, and hard things. Examples: 碗 bowl, 破 break, 碰 touch, 研 grind, 礎 foundation stone.

Big. It began as a picture of a person standing facing forward. As a radical it hardly carries meaning: 太 very, 天 sky, 夫 man, 失 lose. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning.

Person. It began as a side view of a person standing. As a radical it is mostly a shape: 今 modern, 会 meet, 以 by, 从 from, 众 crowd. When the meaning really is person, it is usually written 亻 on the left.
Ice, a compressed form of 仌, written as two dots on the left side. It brings cold. Examples: 冷 cold, 凉 cool, 冰 ice, 净 clean. It has two dots, where the water radical 氵 has three.
Body. It sits over the top-left of a character. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 屋 building, 层 layer, 局 bureau, 尺 ruler, 展 open.
This is the number ten, a cross. As a radical it is not a clue to meaning: 半 half, 午 noon, 南 south and 千 thousand have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Field. It began as a picture of a field divided into four sections. As a radical it is mostly a shape: 男 man, 画 picture, 留 stay, 由 cause. Only a few, such as 界 boundary, plausibly have to do with fields.
Child. It began as a picture of a baby. On the left or bottom, it brings children and descendants. Examples: 孩 baby, 孫 grandchild, 學 learning, 字 character. In 季 and 存 it is only part of the shape.

The simplified form of 金 (gold, metal), written on the left; the same radical as 釒 in traditional characters. It brings metal, money and metal objects. Examples: 钱 money, 钟 clock, 铁 iron, 银 silver, 锁 lock.

King. As a radical it is mostly a shape, written on the left. The examples have no clear theme: 球 ball, 玩 play with, 理 science, 环 bracelet. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning.
A squeezed form of 食 (food, eat), written on the left side, the simplified form of 飠. It brings food and eating. Examples: 饭 meal, 饱 satisfied, 饮 swallow, 饺 dumpling, 饼 rice-cake.

A squeezed form of 食 (food, eat), written on the left side. It brings food and eating. Examples: 飯 meal, 飽 satisfied, 飲 swallow, 餃 dumpling, 餅 rice-cake. 饣 is the same radical in simplified characters.

Short-tailed bird. It began as a picture of a short-tailed bird. On the right, it brings birds, as in 雞 chicken. Elsewhere it is often just a shape to file characters under, or the sound part, as in 雖 although, 隻 only and 雜 mix, so it is not a reliable clue to meaning.

The simplified form of 貝 (shell, money), written on the left or bottom. It brings money, trade and value. Examples: 贵 expensive, 费 expenses, 资 wealth, 货 goods, 赢 win. 貝 is the same radical in traditional characters.

The simplified form of 頁 (head, page), usually on the right. It brings the head and face. Examples: 颜 face, 顺 submit, 领 neck, 顾 look back, 题 forehead. 頁 is the same radical in traditional characters. In 颗 it is the sound part.
Inch. As a radical it is mostly a shape, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 对 correct, 封 envelope, 导 direct, 專 concentrated. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
This is the number eight, two strokes. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning: 六 six, 公 fair, 共 all, 其 his, 具 tool have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.

Child, as a radical placed at the bottom. In 兒 it is the meaning part, but elsewhere it is mostly a shape to file characters under, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 先 first, 元 first, 光 light, 兄 elder brother.

The left half of 行, which represents a street intersection seen from above. Written on the left, it brings walking and going. Examples: 往 go, 從 from, 很 very, 後 after. It looks like 亻 but is unrelated.

It began as a mouth with breath coming out. As a radical it gives no clue to meaning: 書, 會, 最, 更 and 替 are all just filed here. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under. Do not confuse it with 日 (sun).

Spear. It began as an ancient weapon with a single blade. As a radical it is mostly a shape, not a clue to meaning. Examples: 我 I, 或 or, 成 accomplish, 戲 play. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
Walk, run. It began as a picture of a running man. On the left or bottom-left, it brings walking, running and going. Examples: 起 start, 超 surpass, 越 exceed, 趕 pursue, 趣 interest.
A single slash stroke. As a radical it carries no clue to meaning: 么, 乐, 久, 义 and 乘 have nothing in common. Here it is mostly a shape to file characters under.
